The prime minister chairs the Cabinet of Japan and has the ability to select and dismiss its ministers of state. The prime minister also serves as the commander-in-chief of the Japan Self Defence Forces.

results.title: Shinzo Abe | Biography, Assassination, & Facts | Britannica
results.content: Abe became Japan’s longest-serving prime minister in November 2019, when his time in office eclipsed that of Kōshaku Katsura Tarō, who had served three nonconsecutive terms in the early 20th century. In August 2020 Abe announced that he would resign as prime minister because of a recurrence of ulcerative colitis, although he remained in office in a caretaker capacity pending the selection of a successor. On September 14, 2020, Yoshihide Suga, Abe’s chief cabinet secretary, was chosen as the new [...] Shinzo Abe served as Japan's prime minister for two terms. His first term was from 2006 to 2007. After a period out of office, he returned to power in December 2012 and remained prime minister until August 2020, becoming Japan's longest-serving prime minister. Abe resigned due to a recurrence of ulcerative colitis. He was succeeded by Yoshihide Suga. While delivering a campaign speech in July 2022, Abe was assassinated. [...] A conservative, Abe aimed to strengthen ties with the United States and pursue a more assertive foreign policy. In 2006, Abe became the country’s first prime minister born after World War II and its youngest since the war. In September 2012, he was again elected leader of the LDP. Abe launched an economic program dubbed “Abenomics”. He became Japan’s longest-serving prime minister in November 2019. On July 8, 2022, Abe was assassinated while delivering a campaign speech.
